notes: Class XI theory: Time 3 Hours, Total Marks 70; practical 30 (Volumetric Analysis 08, Salt Analysis 08, Content Based Experiment 06, Project Work 04, Class record and viva 04).

Each unit is printed as one comma-separated list of (NCERT section) topics with no chapter level, so each unit has one chapter repeating the unit title and topics[] = the comma-separated items as printed (protected phrases where a comma is inside one item, e.g. 'Relationship between Equilibrium Constant K, Reaction Quotient Q and Gibbs Energy G').
Question paper design: 'No chapter wise weightage is provided, however, care to be taken to cover all the chapters.' — the per-unit marks are those printed in the course-structure table.

Qualitative-analysis cation/anion lists in the practical syllabus are typeset in bold math-italic (non-BMP) characters, e.g. '𝑷𝒃𝟐+'; they are copied verbatim, with charges flattened onto the line as the text layer gives them (Pb²⁺ reads 'Pb2+', CO₃²⁻ reads 'CO3 2−'). (Main-thread fix 2026-10-12: an earlier decoding turned these into U+FFFD and dropped them.)
Practicals: the main practical syllabus only (sections A-F/K + suggested projects); the reduced list for visually challenged students is not copied.

Unit 5 is titled 'Thermodynamics' in the detailed syllabus but 'Chemical Thermodynamics' in the course-structure table; unit 8 is 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques' (table: 'Organic Chemistry: Some basic Principles and Techniques').

FORMATIVE-ONLY units (source: 'included in the syllabus but will be assessed only formatively ... Relevant NCERT textual material is enclosed for reference'): 's & p Block Elements' and 'The Gaseous State' (formativeOnly: true, no marks). The enclosed NCERT material is the CBSE Reading Material PDF Chemistry_SecP2_2026-27_RM.pdf (downloaded, 'Adapted from NCERT textbook of class XI 2006 edition reprinted edition pre rationalization').

practicals.heading: A.Basic Laboratory Techniques
items: 1. Cutting glass tube and glass rod
2. Bending a glass tube
3. Drawing out a glass jet
4. Boring a cork

practicals.heading: B.Characterization and Purification of Chemical Substances
items: 1. Determination of melting point of an organic compound.
2. Determination of boiling point of an organic compound.
3. Crystallization of impure sample of any one of the following: Alum, Copper Sulphate, Benzoic Acid.

practicals.heading: C.Experiments based on pH
items: 1. Any one of the following experiments:
Determination of pH of some solutions obtained from fruit juices, solution of known and varied concentrations of acids, bases and salts using pH paper or universal indicator.
Comparing the pH of solutions of strong and weak acids of same concentration.
Study the pH change in the titration of a strong base using a universal indicator.
2. Study the pH change by common-ion in case of weak acids and weak bases.

practicals.heading: D.Chemical Equilibrium
items: Any one of the following experiments:
Study the shift in equilibrium between ferric ions and thiocyanate ions by increasing/decreasing the concentration of either of the ions.
Study the shift in equilibrium between [Co(H2O)6]2+ and chloride ions by changing the concentration of either of the ions.

practicals.heading: E.Quantitative Estimation
items: 1. Using a mechanical balance/electronic balance.
2. Preparation of standard solution of Oxalic acid.
3. Determination of strength of a given solution of Sodium hydroxide by titrating it against standard solution of Oxalic acid.
4. Preparation of standard solution of Sodium carbonate.
5. Determination of strength of a given solution of hydrochloric acid by titrating it against standard Sodium Carbonate solution.

practicals.heading: F.Qualitative Analysis
items: 1. Determination of one anion and one cation in a given salt Cations: 𝑷𝒃𝟐+,𝑪𝒖𝟐+, 𝑨𝒍𝟑+, 𝑭𝒆𝟑+,𝑴𝒏𝟐+, 𝑵𝒊𝟐+, 𝒁𝒏𝟐+, 𝑪𝒐𝟐+, 𝑪𝒂𝟐+, 𝑺𝒓𝟐+, 𝑩𝒂𝟐+, 𝑴𝒈𝟐+, 𝑵𝑯𝟒
Anions: 𝑪𝑶𝟑 𝟐−,𝐒𝟐− , 𝐒𝐎𝟑 𝟐−, 𝑵𝑶𝟑 −, 𝑵𝑶𝟐 − , 𝐂𝐥−, 𝐁𝐫−, 𝐈− ,𝑺𝑶𝟒 𝟐−, 𝑷𝑶𝟒 𝟑− , 𝐂𝐇𝟑 𝐂𝐎𝐎− (Note: Insoluble salts excluded)
2. Detection of -Nitrogen, Sulphur, Chlorine in organic compounds.

practicals.heading: PROJECTS
items: Scientific investigations involving laboratory testing and collecting information from other sources. A few suggested Projects
a) Checking the bacterial contamination in drinking water by testing sulphide ion
b) Study of the methods of purification of water

c) Testing the hardness, presence of Iron, Fluoride, Chloride, etc., depending upon the regional variation in drinking water and study of causes of presence of these ions above permissible limit (if any).
d) Investigation of the foaming capacity of different washing soaps and the effect of addition of Sodium carbonate on it
e) Study the acidity of different samples of tea leaves.
f) Determination of the rate of evaporation of different liquids
g) Study the effect of acids and bases on the tensile strength of fibers.
h) Study of acidity of fruit and vegetable juices.
